description: Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean GOT taken over all lab records.

c.request: For each patient in `Laboratory`, show the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the overall average GOT. Use that one overall figure for every patient, and return nothing if it is missing. Ignore missing values. Sort by the difference, highest first with missing differences last, return the top 10, and don't round. Compare each patient's average GOT with the mean GOT taken over all lab records.
c.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(GOT) AS avg_got FROM Laboratory), patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID) SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc, p.avg_got - o.avg_got AS got_difference FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE o.avg_got IS NOT NULL ORDER BY got_difference IS NULL, got_difference DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For each patient with laboratory records, return the patient ID, average non-null GOT, average non-null RBC, and the patient’s average GOT minus the average non-null GOT across all laboratory records; return no rows if the overall average is null, sort by the difference descending with null differences last, and limit to 10 rows without rounding
b.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(GOT) AS avg_got FROM Laboratory) SELECT l.ID AS patient_id, AVG(l.GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(l.RBC) AS avg_rbc, AVG(l.GOT) - overall.avg_got AS got_difference FROM Laboratory AS l CROSS JOIN overall WHERE overall.avg_got IS NOT NULL GROUP BY l.ID ORDER BY got_difference IS NULL, got_difference DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each patient in `Laboratory` (grouped by `ID`), give the patient ID, their average GOT, their average RBC, and their average GOT minus the average GOT across all laboratory records. That single overall figure is used for every patient, and if it is missing, return no rows. Ignore missing values in all averages. Show the 10 patients with the largest difference, highest first with missing differences last, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(GOT) AS overall_got FROM Laboratory), patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS average_got, AVG(RBC) AS average_rbc FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID) SELECT p.ID, p.average_got, p.average_rbc, p.average_got - o.overall_got AS got_difference FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE o.overall_got IS NOT NULL ORDER BY got_difference IS NULL, got_difference DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each patient in `Laboratory`, show the patient ID, average GOT, average RBC, and the patient’s average GOT minus the mean GOT across all lab records. Ignore missing values, return nothing if the overall mean GOT is missing, and use that same overall mean for every patient. Sort by the difference from highest to lowest, with missing differences last. Return the top 10 without rounding.
d.sql: WITH overall AS (SELECT AVG(GOT) AS mean_got FROM Laboratory), patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(GOT) AS avg_got, AVG(RBC) AS avg_rbc FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID) SELECT p.ID, p.avg_got, p.avg_rbc, p.avg_got - o.mean_got AS got_difference FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE o.mean_got IS NOT NULL ORDER BY got_difference IS NULL, got_difference DESC LIMIT 10;
